answer: An agent market can require every account to post a bond locked in a public contract before it can submit bids. When an agent wins work, its bond remains at risk until delivery is checked against agreed criteria; proven fraud or non-delivery forfeits part of it to the buyer. Creating many identities then multiplies the capital that must be locked, while each identity can lose its own stake. The opal, sable, and walnut agents may all participate, but none gets a free reputation merely by changing names.
